definitions.explanation: Actively and persistently seeking or striving for an ideal, goal, or quality. Implies a sustained effort toward something abstract or valued.

examples.japanese: {利益|りえき}を{追求|ついきゅう}する。
{幸福|こうふく}の{追求|ついきゅう}は{人間|にんげん}の{基本的|きほんてき}な{権利|けんり}だ。
examples.english: The pursuit of happiness is a fundamental human right.

examples.japanese: この{職人|しょくにん}は{長年|ながねん}にわたって{品質|ひんしつ}の{追求|ついきゅう}を{続|つづ}けてきた。
examples.english: This craftsman has continued to pursue quality for many years.

notes:
{追求|ついきゅう} is a noun that can function as a suru verb ({追求|ついきゅう}する). It focuses on the pursuit of abstract goals, ideals, or values.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- [goal]を{追求|ついきゅう}する (pursue a goal)
- [goal]の{追求|ついきゅう} (the pursuit of a goal)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {利益|りえき}を{追求|ついきゅう}する (pursue profit)
- {幸福|こうふく}を{追求|ついきゅう}する (pursue happiness)
- {理想|りそう}を{追求|ついきゅう}する (pursue an ideal)
- {品質|ひんしつ}を{追求|ついきゅう}する (pursue quality)

Distinct from {追及|ついきゅう} (holding someone accountable, pressing for answers) and {追究|ついきゅう} (investigating, researching deeply). All three share the same reading but are written with different final kanji and have different meanings.
